affordance_in_statement: The factory's automated rostering system gathers all pairwise scheduling constraints ... It is guaranteed that ... three workers who all mutually conflict with each other ... all three pairs a–b, a–c, and b–c are conflicts.
removal_suggestion: Define each input pair u v as a directed conflict arc u→v, and define a valid certificate as a < b < c with arcs a→b, a→c, and b→c. Keep the same input and output formats and retain the examples, whose listed arcs already have the required forward directions.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats every input conflict as an undirected edge and uses bitset common-neighbor intersections.
Treats every input conflict as an undirected edge and searches sorted adjacency intersections.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: workers who all mutually conflict with each other

common_affordance: Both surviving solutions symmetrize every input pair and therefore solve an undirected-triangle problem rather than a directed ordered-triangle problem.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It performs a cubic scan over a, b, and c and can take too long at n = 2000.
Its candidate enumeration and common-neighbor checking are too slow in the worst case under the given limits.

recommended_edit: Change the conflict relation from implicitly mutual/undirected pairs to directed arcs, explicitly requiring arcs a→b, a→c, and b→c for the certificate; the surviving programs will incorrectly add reverse arcs and can output nonexistent certificates or miss the lexicographically smallest valid one.
